1 | import os
     2 | import json
     3 | import logging
     4 | from typing import Any, Dict
     5 | from groq import AsyncGroq
     6 | from .models import ClientPayload, ActionInstruction
     7 | from .session import get_or_create_session
     8 | 
     9 | logger = logging.getLogger("perceive.llm_client")
    10 | 
    11 | def get_llm_client():
    12 |     provider = os.getenv("LLM_PROVIDER", "groq").lower()
    13 |     if provider == "offline":
    14 |         base_url = os.getenv("OFFLINE_API_BASE", "http://localhost:11434/v1")
    15 |         # Reuse Groq client pointing to local OpenAI-compatible endpoint
    16 |         return AsyncGroq(
    17 |             api_key="offline-local",
    18 |             base_url=base_url,
    19 |         )
    20 |     else:
    21 |         api_key = os.getenv("GROQ_API_KEY")
    22 |         if not api_key:
    23 |             raise ValueError("GROQ_API_KEY environment variable not set")
    24 |         return AsyncGroq(api_key=api_key)
    25 | 
    26 | def _generate_deterministic_test_action(payload: ClientPayload) -> ActionInstruction:
    27 |     """
    28 |     TEST-ONLY scripted action generator — the ONLY thing this replaces is the
    29 |     nondeterministic external Groq call. Everything downstream in main.py's
    30 |     /analyze (hallucination guard against the REAL dom_summary, the
    31 |     server-authoritative risk_tier override, session continuity, the retry
    32 |     loop, audit logging) still runs for real against whatever this returns.
    33 |     Activated ONLY when LLM_PROVIDER=deterministic_test is explicitly set —
    34 |     never the default, never reachable on the demo path by accident (see
    35 |     get_llm_client(), which is the single gate for this).
    36 |     """
    37 |     elements = payload.dom_summary.elements
    38 |     session = get_or_create_session(payload.session_id)
    39 |     already_targeted = {
    40 |         step["action"].get("target_element_id")
    41 |         for step in session.history
    42 |         if step.get("action")
    43 |     }
    44 | 
    45 |     def is_visible(el) -> bool:
    46 |         # dom_summary carries a bounding_box but no explicit `visible` flag —
    47 |         # a display:none element still gets a bounding_box, just zeroed. A
    48 |         # real LLM has the same limited signal; this mock uses it the same
    49 |         # way a competent one should, rather than assuming presence in the
    50 |         # DOM means the element is currently usable.
    51 |         bb = el.bounding_box
    52 |         return bool(bb) and bb.w > 0 and bb.h > 0
    53 | 
    54 |     def find(pred):
    55 |         return next((el for el in elements if pred(el) and is_visible(el)), None)
    56 | 
    57 |     on_checkout_page = find(lambda el: el.label_text and "card number" in el.label_text.lower()) is not None
    58 | 
    59 |     if not on_checkout_page:
    60 |         email_el = find(
    61 |             lambda el: el.label_text
    62 |             and "email" in el.label_text.lower()
    63 |             and el.semantic_token
    64 |             and el.element_id not in already_targeted
    65 |         )
    66 |         if email_el:
    67 |             return ActionInstruction(
    68 |                 type="type",
    69 |                 target_element_id=email_el.element_id,
    70 |                 value=email_el.semantic_token,
    71 |                 risk_tier="safe",
    72 |                 reasoning_short="deterministic test: filling email field with its semantic token",
    73 |             )
    74 |         login_btn = find(lambda el: el.tag.lower() == "button" and el.label_text and "login" in el.label_text.lower())
    75 |         if login_btn and login_btn.element_id not in already_targeted:
    76 |             return ActionInstruction(
    77 |                 type="click",
    78 |                 target_element_id=login_btn.element_id,
    79 |                 value=None,
    80 |                 risk_tier="safe",
    81 |                 reasoning_short="deterministic test: submitting login",
    82 |             )
    83 |     else:
    84 |         pay_btn = find(lambda el: el.tag.lower() == "button" and el.label_text and "pay" in el.label_text.lower())
    85 |         if pay_btn and pay_btn.element_id not in already_targeted:
    86 |             return ActionInstruction(
    87 |                 type="click",
    88 |                 target_element_id=pay_btn.element_id,
    89 |                 value=None,
    90 |                 risk_tier="safe",
    91 |                 reasoning_short="deterministic test: submitting payment using the saved payment method",
    92 |             )
    93 | 
    94 |     return ActionInstruction(
    95 |         type="task_complete",
    96 |         target_element_id=None,
    97 |         value=None,
    98 |         risk_tier="safe",
    99 |         reasoning_short="deterministic test: nothing left to do",
   100 |     )
   101 | 
   102 | 
   103 | async def generate_action(payload: ClientPayload) -> ActionInstruction:
   104 |     if os.getenv("LLM_PROVIDER", "groq").lower() == "deterministic_test":
   105 |         logger.warning(
   106 |             "LLM_PROVIDER=deterministic_test is active — using the scripted "
   107 |             "test-only action generator, NOT the real Groq LLM. This must "
   108 |             "never be set for a demo."
   109 |         )
   110 |         return _generate_deterministic_test_action(payload)
   111 | 
   112 |     session = get_or_create_session(payload.session_id)
   113 |     history_context = session.get_context_string()
   114 | 
   115 |     # llama-3.3-70b-versatile was deprecated by Groq (confirmed live via
   116 |     # /v1/models during this integration pass — no longer returned).
   117 |     # openai/gpt-oss-120b is the currently-available default; still
   118 |     # overridable via MODEL_NAME.
   119 |     model_name = os.getenv("MODEL_NAME", "openai/gpt-oss-120b")
   120 |     client = get_llm_client()
   121 |     
   122 |     # Dev 2->Dev 3 integration fix: models tested against real traffic
   123 |     # (Groq's llama-3.3-70b-versatile is deprecated; openai/gpt-oss-20b and
   124 |     # -120b are the currently available replacements) reliably guessed a
   125 |     # plausible-but-wrong key name ("action" instead of "type") without a
   126 |     # concrete example, failing Pydantic validation 3/3 retries every time.
   127 |     # Adding the literal schema + a worked example fixed this consistently.
   128 |     system_prompt = """You are a highly capable browser automation agent.
   129 | Your task is to analyze the user's instruction and the current state of the webpage (DOM Summary) to determine the next action.
   130 | 
   131 | You MUST output your response as valid JSON with EXACTLY these keys (no other key names, no nesting):
   132 | {
   133 |   "type": "click" | "type" | "scroll" | "wait" | "ask_user_confirmation" | "task_complete" | "task_failed",
   134 |   "target_element_id": "<element_id from dom_summary, or null>",
   135 |   "value": "<text to type, or null — never a real sensitive value>",
   136 |   "risk_tier": "safe" | "risky",
   137 |   "reasoning_short": "<one short sentence>"
   138 | }
   139 | 
   140 | Example (typing into an email field with element_id "0.1"):
   141 | {"type": "type", "target_element_id": "0.1", "value": "[EMAIL_1]", "risk_tier": "safe", "reasoning_short": "Filling in the email field using its semantic token."}
   142 | 
   143 | IMPORTANT: You MUST NEVER output real sensitive values (passwords, card numbers, etc). If interacting with a sensitive field, use the provided `semantic_token` value exactly as given (e.g. "[EMAIL_1]"), never the real underlying value.
   144 | """
   145 |     
   146 |     user_prompt = f"""
   147 | Task Instruction: {payload.task_instruction}
   148 | Step Number: {payload.step_number}
   149 | 
   150 | History:
   151 | {history_context}
   152 | 
   153 | DOM Summary:
   154 | {payload.dom_summary.model_dump_json(indent=2)}
   155 | 
   156 | Detection Confidence Notes:
   157 | {json.dumps([n.model_dump() for n in payload.detection_confidence_notes], indent=2)}
   158 | 
   159 | Determine the next action to take. Output strictly as JSON.
   160 | """
   161 | 
   162 |     response = await client.chat.completions.create(
   163 |         model=model_name,
   164 |         messages=[
   165 |             {"role": "system", "content": system_prompt},
   166 |             {"role": "user", "content": user_prompt}
   167 |         ],
   168 |         temperature=0.0,
   169 |         response_format={"type": "json_object"}
   170 |     )
   171 |     
   172 |     raw_response = response.choices[0].message.content
   173 |     if not raw_response:
   174 |         raise ValueError("Empty response from LLM")
   175 |         
   176 |     action_dict = json.loads(raw_response)
   177 |     # This will be validated by Pydantic in the caller
   178 |     action = ActionInstruction(**action_dict)
   179 |     return action

1 | from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Request
     2 | from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
     3 | from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
     4 | from pydantic import ValidationError
     5 | from typing import Optional
     6 | from .models import ClientPayload, ServerResponse, ActionInstruction
     7 | from .llm_client import generate_action
     8 | from .session import get_or_create_session
     9 | from .logger import log_audit_event
    10 | 
    11 | app = FastAPI(title="Lightweight Browser Agent Backend")
    12 | 
    13 | # Dev 3 -> Dev 4 integration fix: this backend had no CORS middleware at
    14 | # all. A real content-script fetch() from the extension (initiated from the
    15 | # page's own origin, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:9797 for the QuickShop fixture)
    16 | # to this backend (http://127.0.0.1:8000) failed with a generic "Failed to
    17 | # fetch" — confirmed live, reproduced, and fixed by adding this. The other
    18 | # (non-authoritative) backend/ already had this; server/ never did.
    19 | app.add_middleware(
    20 |     CORSMiddleware,
    21 |     allow_origins=["*"],
    22 |     allow_credentials=True,
    23 |     allow_methods=["*"],
    24 |     allow_headers=["*"],
    25 | )
    26 | 
    27 | MAX_RETRIES = 3
    28 | 
    29 | @app.post("/analyze", response_model=ServerResponse)
    30 | async def analyze_step(payload: ClientPayload):
    31 |     """
    32 |     Receives a sanitized payload, fetches session history,
    33 |     calls the reasoning LLM, and enforces ActionInstruction schema.
    34 |     Retries up to MAX_RETRIES on malformed LLM output.
    35 |     """
    36 |     session = get_or_create_session(payload.session_id)
    37 |     
    38 |     # Session continuity defense
    39 |     if payload.step_number > 1 and not session.history:
    40 |         log_audit_event(
    41 |             session_id=payload.session_id,
    42 |             step_number=payload.step_number,
    43 |             instruction=payload.task_instruction,
    44 |             action={"error": "Session continuity broken (fresh UUID mid-task)"},
    45 |             confidence=0.0,
    46 |             payload_notes=[n.model_dump() for n in payload.detection_confidence_notes]
    47 |         )
    48 |         raise HTTPException(
    49 |             status_code=400,
    50 |             detail="Step number > 1 but no session history found. Did the client regenerate session_id mid-task?"
    51 |         )
    52 |     
    53 |     last_exception: Optional[Exception] = None
    54 |     
    55 |     from groq import RateLimitError, APIError
    56 |     
    57 |     for attempt in range(MAX_RETRIES):
    58 |         try:
    59 |             # The LLM client already returns a Pydantic-validated ActionInstruction
    60 |             action = await generate_action(payload)
    61 |             
    62 |             # Additional semantic validation
    63 |             if action.target_element_id:
    64 |                 valid_ids = [el.element_id for el in payload.dom_summary.elements]
    65 |                 if action.target_element_id not in valid_ids:
    66 |                     raise ValueError(f"Hallucinated target_element_id '{action.target_element_id}'. Must be one of {valid_ids}")
    67 |                     
    68 |             # Server-authoritative risk tier override / enforcement
    69 |             # If it's a type action, or interacting with a sensitive field, ensure it's marked risky
    70 |             # This prevents a high-confidence LLM from silently bypassing the safety tier
    71 |             if action.target_element_id:
    72 |                 target_el = next((el for el in payload.dom_summary.elements if el.element_id == action.target_element_id), None)
    73 |                 if target_el and target_el.is_sensitive:
    74 |                     action.risk_tier = "risky"
    75 |             
    76 |             # Record step to session history
    77 |             session.add_step(payload.step_number, payload.task_instruction, action)
    78 |             
    79 |             # Log the event
    80 |             log_audit_event(
    81 |                 session_id=payload.session_id,
    82 |                 step_number=payload.step_number,
    83 |                 instruction=payload.task_instruction,
    84 |                 action=action.model_dump(),
    85 |                 confidence=0.90,
    86 |                 payload_notes=[n.model_dump() for n in payload.detection_confidence_notes]
    87 |             )
    88 |             
    89 |             response = ServerResponse(
    90 |                 session_id=payload.session_id,
    91 |                 step_number=payload.step_number + 1,
    92 |                 action=action,
    93 |                 confidence=0.90 
    94 |             )
    95 |             return response
    96 |             
    97 |         except (ValueError, ValidationError) as ve:
    98 |             # Covers Pydantic ValidationError and our custom ValueError
    99 |             last_exception = ve
   100 |             continue
   101 |         except RateLimitError as e:
   102 |             # Don't blindly retry 429s in a tight loop
   103 |             log_audit_event(
   104 |                 session_id=payload.session_id,
   105 |                 step_number=payload.step_number,
   106 |                 instruction=payload.task_instruction,
   107 |                 action={"error": "Rate limit exceeded (429)"},
   108 |                 confidence=0.0,
   109 |                 payload_notes=[n.model_dump() for n in payload.detection_confidence_notes]
   110 |             )
   111 |             return JSONResponse(
   112 |                 status_code=429,
   113 |                 content={"detail": "Rate limit exceeded. Please wait and try again."},
   114 |                 headers={"Retry-After": "5"}
   115 |             )
   116 |         except Exception as e:
   117 |             # Other errors (e.g., API failures)
   118 |             log_audit_event(
   119 |                 session_id=payload.session_id,
   120 |                 step_number=payload.step_number,
   121 |                 instruction=payload.task_instruction,
   122 |                 action={"error": f"API Failure: {str(e)}"},
   123 |                 confidence=0.0,
   124 |                 payload_notes=[n.model_dump() for n in payload.detection_confidence_notes]
   125 |             )
   126 |             raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=str(e))
   127 |             
   128 |     # If we hit the max retries, fail
   129 |     error_msg = f"Failed to generate a valid action after {MAX_RETRIES} attempts. Last error: {str(last_exception)}"
   130 |     log_audit_event(
   131 |         session_id=payload.session_id,
   132 |         step_number=payload.step_number,
   133 |         instruction=payload.task_instruction,
   134 |         action={"error": error_msg},
   135 |         confidence=0.0,
   136 |         payload_notes=[n.model_dump() for n in payload.detection_confidence_notes]
   137 |     )
   138 |     raise HTTPException(
   139 |         status_code=500, 
   140 |         detail=error_msg
   141 |     )
   142 | 
   143 | @app.exception_handler(ValidationError)
   144 | async def validation_exception_handler(request: Request, exc: ValidationError):
   145 |     """Custom handler to ensure malformed incoming payloads are clearly rejected."""
   146 |     return JSONResponse(
   147 |         status_code=422,
   148 |         content={"detail": exc.errors(), "body": exc.body},
   149 |     )
   150 | 
   151 | @app.get("/health")
   152 | async def health_check():
   153 |     return {"status": "ok"}

1 | from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, model_validator, field_validator
     2 | from typing import List, Optional, Literal
     3 | 
     4 | # -------------------------------------------------------------------
     5 | # Enum-like Literals per PDF Section 4 contracts
     6 | # -------------------------------------------------------------------
     7 | 
     8 | TagType = str
     9 | RoleType = str
    10 | # Canonical representation is STRING ("1"|"2"|"3") — matches the master doc's
    11 | # JSON schema example verbatim. Dev 2's real sensitivity-tiers.js returns a
    12 | # JS *number*; the Dev1->Dev2->Dev3 payload adapter (extension/src/content/
    13 | # dev2-payload.ts) converts number->string explicitly before this schema
    14 | # ever sees it — never relies on implicit JSON coercion (a JS number
    15 | # serializes to a JSON number, which this Literal would reject outright).
    16 | SensitivityTier = Literal["1", "2", "3"]
    17 | # Extended (Dev 2->Dev 3 integration) to include Dev 2's real PII categories
    18 | # that were previously silently unrepresentable here: PHONE, AADHAAR, IFSC,
    19 | # OTP. Not mapped to UNKNOWN/OTHER — Dev 2 already assigns these correct,
    20 | # specific types; dropping that distinction would lose real information the
    21 | # master spec's Tiered Sensitivity Model (§8.1) depends on.
    22 | SensitivityType = Literal[
    23 |     "PASSWORD", "CARD_NUMBER", "EMAIL", "NAME", "AMOUNT", "UNKNOWN",
    24 |     "PHONE", "AADHAAR", "IFSC", "OTP",
    25 | ]
    26 | DetectionMethod = Literal["dom_heuristic", "vision_model", "ocr_regex"]
    27 | ActionType = Literal["click", "type", "scroll", "wait", "ask_user_confirmation", "task_complete", "task_failed"]
    28 | RiskTier = Literal["safe", "risky"]
    29 | 
    30 | # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    31 | # Client -> Server Payload Models
    32 | # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    33 | 
    34 | class BoundingBox(BaseModel):
    35 |     x: int
    36 |     y: int
    37 |     w: int
    38 |     h: int
    39 | 
    40 | class DOMElement(BaseModel):
    41 |     element_id: str
    42 |     tag: TagType
    43 |     # Dev 2's real classifier (dom-heuristics.js) legitimately produces
    44 |     # role: null for most elements (only a minority carry an ARIA/native
    45 |     # role) — this was `role: RoleType` (required, non-nullable) before the
    46 |     # Dev 2->Dev 3 integration, which rejected every real Dev 2 payload with
    47 |     # a validation error. Fixed to match Dev 2's actual output.
    48 |     role: Optional[RoleType] = None
    49 |     label_text: Optional[str] = None
    50 |     is_sensitive: bool
    51 |     sensitivity_tier: Optional[SensitivityTier] = None
    52 |     sensitivity_type: Optional[SensitivityType] = None
    53 |     semantic_token: Optional[str] = None
    54 |     bounding_box: BoundingBox
    55 | 
    56 |     @model_validator(mode='after')
    57 |     def check_sensitive_has_token(self):
    58 |         # Section 8.2: Redaction breaks task utility - Semantic placeholder tokens instead of blind blackout
    59 |         # The server must NEVER receive a real sensitive value in any field.
    60 |         if self.is_sensitive and self.semantic_token is None:
    61 |             # We don't strictly reject missing token if they just blinded it, but we encourage it.
    62 |             pass
    63 |         return self
    64 | 
    65 | class DOMSummary(BaseModel):
    66 |     url: str
    67 |     elements: List[DOMElement]
    68 | 
    69 | class DetectionConfidenceNote(BaseModel):
    70 |     element_id: str
    71 |     confidence: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)
    72 |     method: DetectionMethod
    73 | 
    74 | class ClientPayload(BaseModel):
    75 |     session_id: str
    76 |     task_instruction: str
    77 |     step_number: int
    78 |     dom_summary: DOMSummary
    79 |     redacted_image_base64: Optional[str] = None
    80 |     detection_confidence_notes: List[DetectionConfidenceNote] = []
    81 | 
    82 | # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    83 | # Server -> Client Action Response Models
    84 | # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    85 | 
    86 | class ActionInstruction(BaseModel):
    87 |     type: ActionType
    88 |     target_element_id: Optional[str] = None
    89 |     value: Optional[str] = None
    90 |     risk_tier: RiskTier
    91 |     reasoning_short: str
    92 | 
    93 |     @field_validator("risk_tier", mode="before")
    94 |     @classmethod
    95 |     def reject_non_enum_risk_tier(cls, v):
    96 |         if v not in ("safe", "risky"):
    97 |             raise ValueError(
    98 |                 f"risk_tier must be 'safe' or 'risky', got {v!r} "
    99 |                 f"(type {type(v).__name__}) — numeric conversion is client-side only, "
   100 |                 f"backend does not coerce"
   101 |             )
   102 |         return v
   103 | 
   104 |     @model_validator(mode='after')
   105 |     def check_required_fields_based_on_type(self):
   106 |         if self.type in ["click", "type"] and not self.target_element_id:
   107 |             raise ValueError(f"target_element_id is required for action type '{self.type}'")
   108 |         if self.type == "type" and self.value is None:
   109 |             raise ValueError("value is required for 'type' action")
   110 |         return self
   111 | 
   112 | class ServerResponse(BaseModel):
   113 |     session_id: str
   114 |     step_number: int
   115 |     action: ActionInstruction
   116 |     confidence: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)

1 | from typing import Dict, List, Any
     2 | from .models import ActionInstruction
     3 | 
     4 | class Session:
     5 |     def __init__(self, session_id: str):
     6 |         self.session_id = session_id
     7 |         self.history: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
     8 | 
     9 |     def add_step(self, step_number: int, instruction: str, action: ActionInstruction):
    10 |         self.history.append({
    11 |             "step_number": step_number,
    12 |             "instruction": instruction,
    13 |             "action": action.model_dump()
    14 |         })
    15 |         
    16 |     def get_context_string(self) -> str:
    17 |         if not self.history:
    18 |             return "No previous steps in this session."
    19 |         
    20 |         context = "Previous steps taken:\n"
    21 |         for step in self.history:
    22 |             context += f"Step {step['step_number']}: Intended to '{step['instruction']}'. Executed action: {step['action']['type']} on {step['action'].get('target_element_id', 'N/A')}\n"
    23 |         return context
    24 | 
    25 | # Simple in-memory store
    26 | _sessions: Dict[str, Session] = {}
    27 | 
    28 | def get_or_create_session(session_id: str) -> Session:
    29 |     if session_id not in _sessions:
    30 |         _sessions[session_id] = Session(session_id)
    31 |     return _sessions[session_id]
    32 | 
    33 | def clear_session(session_id: str):
    34 |     if session_id in _sessions:
    35 |         del _sessions[session_id]

    18 |         api_key = os.getenv("GROQ_API_KEY")
    19 |         if not api_key:
    20 |             raise ValueError("GROQ_API_KEY environment variable not set")
    21 |         return AsyncGroq(api_key=api_key)

    23 | async def generate_action(payload: ClientPayload) -> ActionInstruction:
    24 |     session = get_or_create_session(payload.session_id)
    25 |     history_context = session.get_context_string()
    26 |     
    27 |     model_name = os.getenv("MODEL_NAME", "llama-3.3-70b-versatile")
    28 |     client = get_llm_client()
    29 |     
    30 |     system_prompt = """You are a highly capable browser automation agent.
    31 | Your task is to analyze the user's instruction and the current state of the webpage (DOM Summary) to determine the next action.
    32 | You MUST output your response as valid JSON matching the ActionInstruction schema.
    33 | IMPORTANT: You MUST NEVER output real sensitive values (passwords, card numbers, etc). If interacting with a sensitive field, use the provided `semantic_token`.
    34 | """
    35 |     
    36 |     user_prompt = f"""
    37 | Task Instruction: {payload.task_instruction}
    38 | Step Number: {payload.step_number}
    39 | 
    40 | History:
    41 | {history_context}
    42 | 
    43 | DOM Summary:
    44 | {payload.dom_summary.model_dump_json(indent=2)}
    45 | 
    46 | Detection Confidence Notes:
    47 | {json.dumps([n.model_dump() for n in payload.detection_confidence_notes], indent=2)}
    48 | 
    49 | Determine the next action to take. Output strictly as JSON.
    50 | """
    51 | 
    52 |     response = await client.chat.completions.create(
    53 |         model=model_name,
    54 |         messages=[
    55 |             {"role": "system", "content": system_prompt},
    56 |             {"role": "user", "content": user_prompt}
    57 |         ],
    58 |         temperature=0.0,
    59 |         response_format={"type": "json_object"}
    60 |     )

     7 | from .session import get_or_create_session
     8 | from .logger import log_audit_event
     9 | 
    10 | app = FastAPI(title="Lightweight Browser Agent Backend")
    11 | 
    12 | MAX_RETRIES = 3
    13 | 
    14 | @app.post("/analyze", response_model=ServerResponse)
    15 | async def analyze_step(payload: ClientPayload):
    16 |     """
    17 |     Receives a sanitized payload, fetches session history,
    18 |     calls the reasoning LLM, and enforces ActionInstruction schema.
    19 |     Retries up to MAX_RETRIES on malformed LLM output.
    20 |     """
    21 |     session = get_or_create_session(payload.session_id)
    22 |     
    23 |     # Session continuity defense
    24 |     if payload.step_number > 1 and not session.history:
    25 |         log_audit_event(
    26 |             session_id=payload.session_id,
    27 |             step_number=payload.step_number,
    28 |             instruction=payload.task_instruction,
    29 |             action={"error": "Session continuity broken (fresh UUID mid-task)"},
    30 |             confidence=0.0,
    31 |             payload_notes=[n.model_dump() for n in payload.detection_confidence_notes]
    32 |         )
    33 |         raise HTTPException(
    34 |             status_code=400,
    35 |             detail="Step number > 1 but no session history found. Did the client regenerate session_id mid-task?"
    36 |         )
    37 |     
    38 |     last_exception: Optional[Exception] = None
    39 |     
    40 |     from groq import RateLimitError, APIError
    41 |     
    42 |     for attempt in range(MAX_RETRIES):
    43 |         try:
    44 |             # The LLM client already returns a Pydantic-validated ActionInstruction
    45 |             action = await generate_action(payload)
    46 |             
    47 |             # Additional semantic validation
    48 |             if action.target_element_id:
    49 |                 valid_ids = [el.element_id for el in payload.dom_summary.elements]
    50 |                 if action.target_element_id not in valid_ids:
    51 |                     raise ValueError(f"Hallucinated target_element_id '{action.target_element_id}'. Must be one of {valid_ids}")
    52 |                     
    53 |             # Server-authoritative risk tier override / enforcement
    54 |             # If it's a type action, or interacting with a sensitive field, ensure it's marked risky
    55 |             # This prevents a high-confidence LLM from silently bypassing the safety tier
    56 |             if action.target_element_id:
    57 |                 target_el = next((el for el in payload.dom_summary.elements if el.element_id == action.target_element_id), None)
    58 |                 if target_el and target_el.is_sensitive:
    59 |                     action.risk_tier = "risky"
    60 |             
    61 |             # Record step to session history
    62 |             session.add_step(payload.step_number, payload.task_instruction, action)
    63 |             
    64 |             # Log the event
    65 |             log_audit_event(
    66 |                 session_id=payload.session_id,
    67 |                 step_number=payload.step_number,
    68 |                 instruction=payload.task_instruction,
    69 |                 action=action.model_dump(),
    70 |                 confidence=0.90,
    71 |                 payload_notes=[n.model_dump() for n in payload.detection_confidence_notes]
    72 |             )
    73 |             
    74 |             response = ServerResponse(
    75 |                 session_id=payload.session_id,
    76 |                 step_number=payload.step_number + 1,
    77 |                 action=action,
    78 |                 confidence=0.90 
    79 |             )
    80 |             return response
    81 |             
    82 |         except (ValueError, ValidationError) as ve:
    83 |             # Covers Pydantic ValidationError and our custom ValueError
    84 |             last_exception = ve
    85 |             continue
    86 |         except RateLimitError as e:
    87 |             # Don't blindly retry 429s in a tight loop
    88 |             log_audit_event(
    89 |                 session_id=payload.session_id,
    90 |                 step_number=payload.step_number,
    91 |                 instruction=payload.task_instruction,
    92 |                 action={"error": "Rate limit exceeded (429)"},
    93 |                 confidence=0.0,
    94 |                 payload_notes=[n.model_dump() for n in payload.detection_confidence_notes]
    95 |             )
    96 |             return JSONResponse(
    97 |                 status_code=429,
    98 |                 content={"detail": "Rate limit exceeded. Please wait and try again."},
    99 |                 headers={"Retry-After": "5"}
   100 |             )
   101 |         except Exception as e:
   102 |             # Other errors (e.g., API failures)
   103 |             log_audit_event(
   104 |                 session_id=payload.session_id,
   105 |                 step_number=payload.step_number,
   106 |                 instruction=payload.task_instruction,
   107 |                 action={"error": f"API Failure: {str(e)}"},
   108 |                 confidence=0.0,
   109 |                 payload_notes=[n.model_dump() for n in payload.detection_confidence_notes]
   110 |             )
   111 |             raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=str(e))
   112 |             
   113 |     # If we hit the max retries, fail
   114 |     error_msg = f"Failed to generate a valid action after {MAX_RETRIES} attempts. Last error: {str(last_exception)}"
   115 |     log_audit_event(
   116 |         session_id=payload.session_id,
   117 |         step_number=payload.step_number,
   118 |         instruction=payload.task_instruction,
   119 |         action={"error": error_msg},
   120 |         confidence=0.0,
   121 |         payload_notes=[n.model_dump() for n in payload.detection_confidence_notes]
   122 |     )
   123 |     raise HTTPException(
   124 |         status_code=500, 
   125 |         detail=error_msg
   126 |     )

     2 | from typing import List, Optional, Literal

     4 | # -------------------------------------------------------------------
     5 | # Enum-like Literals per PDF Section 4 contracts
     6 | # -------------------------------------------------------------------
     7 | 
     8 | TagType = str

    10 | SensitivityTier = Literal["1", "2", "3"]
    11 | SensitivityType = Literal["PASSWORD", "CARD_NUMBER", "EMAIL", "NAME", "AMOUNT", "UNKNOWN"]
    12 | DetectionMethod = Literal["dom_heuristic", "vision_model", "ocr_regex"]

    14 | RiskTier = Literal["safe", "risky"]

    16 | # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    17 | # Client -> Server Payload Models
    18 | # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    19 | 
    20 | class BoundingBox(BaseModel):
    21 |     x: int
    22 |     y: int
    23 |     w: int
    24 |     h: int
    25 |

    27 |     element_id: str
    28 |     tag: TagType

    31 |     is_sensitive: bool

    38 |     def check_sensitive_has_token(self):
    39 |         # Section 8.2: Redaction breaks task utility - Semantic placeholder tokens instead of blind blackout
    40 |         # The server must NEVER receive a real sensitive value in any field.
    41 |         if self.is_sensitive and self.semantic_token is None:
    42 |             # We don't strictly reject missing token if they just blinded it, but we encourage it.
    43 |             pass
    44 |         return self
    45 | 
    46 | class DOMSummary(BaseModel):
    47 |     url: str
    48 |     elements: List[DOMElement]
    49 | 
    50 | class DetectionConfidenceNote(BaseModel):

    53 |     method: DetectionMethod
    54 | 
    55 | class ClientPayload(BaseModel):
    56 |     session_id: str
    57 |     task_instruction: str
    58 |     step_number: int
    59 |     dom_summary: DOMSummary
    60 |     redacted_image_base64: Optional[str] = None
    61 |     detection_confidence_notes: List[DetectionConfidenceNote] = []
    62 | 
    63 | # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    64 | # Server -> Client Action Response Models
    65 | # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    66 | 
    67 | class ActionInstruction(BaseModel):
    68 |     type: ActionType

    70 |     value: Optional[str] = None
    71 |     risk_tier: RiskTier
    72 |     reasoning_short: str
    73 | 
    74 |     @field_validator("risk_tier", mode="before")
    75 |     @classmethod
    76 |     def reject_non_enum_risk_tier(cls, v):
    77 |         if v not in ("safe", "risky"):
    78 |             raise ValueError(
    79 |                 f"risk_tier must be 'safe' or 'risky', got {v!r} "
    80 |                 f"(type {type(v).__name__}) — numeric conversion is client-side only, "
    81 |                 f"backend does not coerce"

    83 |         return v
    84 |

    89 |         if self.type == "type" and self.value is None:

     4 | class Session:
     5 |     def __init__(self, session_id: str):
     6 |         self.session_id = session_id
     7 |         self.history: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
     8 | 
     9 |     def add_step(self, step_number: int, instruction: str, action: ActionInstruction):
    10 |         self.history.append({
    11 |             "step_number": step_number,
    12 |             "instruction": instruction,
    13 |             "action": action.model_dump()
    14 |         })
    15 |         
    16 |     def get_context_string(self) -> str:
    17 |         if not self.history:
    18 |             return "No previous steps in this session."
    19 |         
    20 |         context = "Previous steps taken:\n"
    21 |         for step in self.history:
    22 |             context += f"Step {step['step_number']}: Intended to '{step['instruction']}'. Executed action: {step['action']['type']} on {step['action'].get('target_element_id', 'N/A')}\n"
    23 |         return context
    24 | 
    25 | # Simple in-memory store
    26 | _sessions: Dict[str, Session] = {}
    27 | 
    28 | def get_or_create_session(session_id: str) -> Session:
    29 |     if session_id not in _sessions:
    30 |         _sessions[session_id] = Session(session_id)
    31 |     return _sessions[session_id]
    32 | 
    33 | def clear_session(session_id: str):
    34 |     if session_id in _sessions:
    35 |         del _sessions[session_id]
